title: Systemic lupus erythematosus
bottleneck: Lupus is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease with flares, organ-threatening nephritis, and no reliable biomarker to guide therapy; treatment still leans on broad immunosuppression with corticosteroids, and many patients cycle through drugs without achieving durable remission.
why_it_blocks: Lupus strikes young women disproportionately and causes cumulative organ damage; trial-and-error immunosuppression is a poor substitute for targeted, curative therapy.
current_state: CAR-T cell therapy has induced drug-free remission in small lupus case series, a striking signal, and new biologics are approved. Whether CAR-T or other approaches deliver lasting cures at scale is untested. The heterogeneity of lupus, with diverse autoantibodies and organ involvement, makes one-size-fits-all therapy impossible. Biomarker-driven trial designs and immune-reset strategies like CAR-T represent the field's best hopes for moving beyond chronic immunosuppression.
